name: Perfection
caption: A wrestler who never tires of calling himself perfect, who lost the promotion's first world title match and then went on to win, lose, and reclaim the Emerald City Championship across both of the fed's seasons.

identity.note: A different "Perfection" is already held under cswa (perfection-cswa), a one-off 1996 appearance with no shared vitals, moniker, or era; "Perfection"/"Mr. Perfect" is a common archetype ring name in this hobby and no evidence ties the two.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011), "Chain Reaction 4" (7 January 2012), "IWF Presents: Surge!" (22 July 2012), "Chain Reaction 10" (18 September 2012), the "King of the Mountain: Perfection (C) vs. Leyenda de Ocho" promo exchange (27-30 January 2013), and "IWF S02E01 King of the Mountain" (17 February 2013)

name: Dol-FAN!
caption: A masked Miami Dolphins-themed entrant beaten by Perfection in IWF's very first match.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011)

name: Kerry Kuroyama
caption: A young wrestler trained at "The Dojo" who won his debut match on IWF's first show and departed the fed years later in a farewell match, bound for a wrestling contract in Japan.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011, defeating David 'The Bird' Gilbride), "IWF Presents: Surge!" (22 July 2012, named as a competitor in a match against Erik Mateo not separately structured), and "IWF S02E01 King of the Mountain" (17 February 2013, his own farewell match against Scott Douglas before departing for a contract in Japan)
NFW's own backstage database (accession 0159), bio 11137
tenures.note: Dated from the fed's own record of its matches (9 shows). Joined to this record on the verified map of record (NFW-A) and the card's own text.

name: David 'The Bird' Gilbride
caption: An entrant with a flapping bird gimmick who intentionally rolled Kerry Kuroyama on top of himself to lose IWF's second match of the night.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011)

name: 'Sub Pop' Scott Douglas
caption: A hometown Seattle wrestler who won IWF's first match against a bigger opponent, fell short of the promotion's first world title at its own debut pay-per-view, and returned more than a year later to send his old rival off with a win in the fed's own Season 2 premiere.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011, defeating "The Fallen Angel" Stephen Waltz), "Chain Reaction 4" (7 January 2012, the Emerald City Championship tournament final), and "IWF S02E01 King of the Mountain" (17 February 2013, defeating Kerry Kuroyama in Kuroyama's own farewell match)

name: Colt-FAN!
caption: A hobbled NFL-fan gimmick wrestler forced into a second match the same night he was already beaten up, and tapped out to Mary-Lynn Mayweather in IWF's first-ever main event.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 1" (18 November 2011)

name: Vizier ta Seti
caption: IWF's first-ever Emerald City Champion, crowned in an eight-man tournament and dethroned seven months later at the fed's own supershow.

tenures.source: IWF's own "Chain Reaction 4" (7 January 2012, winning the vacant Emerald City Championship) and the fed's own Emerald City Championship title history (title lost 22 July 2012 at "IWF Presents: Surge!")
the fed's own served show documents, read start to finish — this character is named and staged directly in NFW's own results text

The Commission's own sign-up thread, card release and results podcast for Fly Me to the Moon (May and June 2012): billed as the IWF Emerald City Champion, he answered Hornet's open challenge and lost the main event.

name: Steve 'Axion' Jackson
caption: A Chicago wrestler who made a handful of appearances for IWF over the years before entering the fed's own Season 2 title tournament.

identity.note: A wrestler billed only "Steve Jackson" (no moniker) is already held under wia, an unrelated federation with no shared vitals, moniker, or era found; treated as a coincidental name reuse.

tenures.source: IWF's own "IWF S02E01 King of the Mountain" (17 February 2013), which describes him as having "made a few appearances in the IWF over the past few years" without dating any of them

The Commission's own sign-up lists, roleplay threads and roster bio: listed as Axion Jackson (IWF), entered in the Organised Chaos triangle match, booked on the Wrestlesaurus Rex pilot and entered on the Unlucky For Some 2013 tour as El Hacha of Los Planetarios.

notes: Also wrestled for the Intergalactic Championship Commission (igc) under the same name and moniker, as the Commission's own sign-up lists tag him "Axion Jackson (IWF)"; the Commission's roster bio is served in the igc wing. Graded a merge at primary-source (an original character carried by its own handler across promotions).

name: El Cabron
caption: A masked, goat-costumed luchador who debuted for IWF in the fed's own inaugural Mount Rainier Championship rumble match.

tenures.source: IWF's own "IWF S02E01 King of the Mountain" (17 February 2013), which states "not much was given to us on this individual in the way of a background"

name: Eddie Whisky
caption: A tall, bluster-prone heel who calls the IWF his new pet project and feuds with Mary-Lynn Mayweather over her wins, from Chain Reaction 6 to a no-cheating match at Surge.

tenures.source: The fed's own cards, notices and roleplays on its forum (2011-11-02 to 2013-05-19)

name: Derrick Allen
caption: A Seattle native, the older brother of Courtney Allen and Scott Douglas's former best friend, who returned to start his IWF career against Erik Mateo at Chain Reaction 7; later billed as "ADD" Derrick Allen.

tenures.source: The fed's own cards, notices and roleplays on its forum (2012-02-12 to 2013-03-06)

name: Courtney Allen
caption: Scott Douglas's girlfriend and in-fiction production aide and Derrick Allen's sister; seriously hurt at Surge in a chair attack in which the fed's own news story implicates both men.

tenures.source: The fed's own cards, notices and roleplays on its forum (2011-11-10 to 2013-03-06)

name: The Minstrel
caption: A masked villain in a Greek comedy mask whose catchphrase is that his work is "no laughing matter"; he debuted at Chain Reaction 7, attacked Go-Go Spectacular backstage and then fought her at Chain Reaction 8 and Surge, and later fought Mary-Lynn Mayweather.

tenures.source: The fed's own cards, notices and roleplays on its forum (2012-03-06 to 2013-01-20)

name: Go-Go Spectacular
caption: A nineteen-year-old masked lucha libre wrestler from El Paso, Texas, who speaks of a transplanted heart and debuted at Chain Reaction 7 in a triple threat with Mary-Lynn Mayweather and Johnny Niles before The Minstrel attacked her.

tenures.source: The fed's own cards, notices and roleplays on its forum (2012-03-07 to 2012-09-22)

name: Spooky Doom
caption: A short, wide-shouldered luchador in a hooded bodysuit with a black Pac-Man ghost across the chest, a self-styled "Grim Reaper thingy" and the nephew of a legendary undead wrestler; he faced Johnny Niles at Chain Reaction 8, Johnny Niles and Eddie Patton at Surge and Leyenda de Ocho at Chain Reaction 9.

caption: A British aristocrat's son billed from Buckingham, UK, who wrestles in a three-piece suit with a team of "trainers"; he was one of the fed's newest signees of mid-2012, faced Kerry Kuroyama at Chain Reaction 10 and teamed with Johnny Niles at Chain Reaction 11.

caption: A big West Texan billed from El Paso and living in East Harlem, built on the 1980s Dusty Rhodes and Ric Flair formula, who faced Erik Mateo at Chain Reaction 2.

caption: A masked wrestler billed as Mr. Wrestling VIII; he opposed Stephen Waltz on The Experience and Derrick Allen at Chain Reaction 8.

name: Curtis Reeds
caption: A 6'8" bald, scarred power wrestler from Phoenix, Arizona, with a devil-head tattoo and a Torture Rack finisher; his bio card is in the fed's Season 2 roster.

caption: Pain GRILLE's silent, monkey-tailed cousin and lackey, who carries the French flag at his side and fights as one half of Retour des Centres.

caption: A man called the Gladiator, working a factory shift years after he left wrestling, whom his old manager visits with the name of a contact at the IWF; a short in-character story in the fed's airtime forum.
